question: Do either distributed demand accumulation or slow selling-pressure exhaustion create a broad, causal A-share event family worth full candlestick review?

shared_contract.history: exact prior completed market sessions only; require contiguous 60-session stock history and unchanged corporate-action coordinate lineage
shared_contract.universe: registered MAIN and CHINEXT non-ST hard-valid, tradable, identity-valid and market-rule-valid rows
shared_contract.signal_bar: completed daily bar; close must not equal the upper price limit
shared_contract.deduplication: keep only the first raw occurrence for the symbol and mechanism after 20 completed market sessions without another raw occurrence
shared_contract.entry: first legal non-upper-limit open in the next three market sessions
shared_contract.target_execution: no earlier than the first stock session after entry, preserving T+1
shared_contract.time_stop: decision after the frozen number of completed market sessions, then first legal sellable open

mothers.economic_claim: A moderate 20-session advance built by repeated small gains and relatively little downside turnover represents distributed accumulation; the first non-extreme, high-close escape above the pre-existing 20-session ceiling is delayed price discovery rather than lottery demand.

After a material decline, five sessions of non-deteriorating lows and lower downside turnover than the preceding five sessions indicate selling-pressure exhaustion; a moderate high-close clearance of the prior-five ceiling is the first new demand takeover.

screen_gate.promotion: Only a mother passing all gates may receive a full plus/minus-six-month chartbook. No union, sign inversion, threshold rescue, or neighboring horizon is allowed in this batch.
